edits.field_name: Excess meal payments over 41 UVT (ET art. 387-1)
edits.current: Where the employer pays a THIRD PARTY for the employee's or their family's meals - a restaurant, own or third-party, or vouchers for food - the payment is deductible for the employer and is NOT income for the employee but for the supplier, PROVIDED the employee's salary does not exceed 310 UVT (COP 16,235,940 per month in 2026). Where the monthly payments exceed 41 UVT (COP 2,147,334 in 2026), THE EXCESS is taxable income of the employee and is withheld as employment income. The instruction guide adds that the rule does not apply to company representation expenses, which remain deductible. Do NOT include amounts already in casilla 36.
edits.proposed: Where the employer pays a THIRD PARTY for the employee's or their family's meals - a restaurant, own or third-party, or vouchers for food - the payment is deductible for the employer and is NOT income for the employee but for the supplier, PROVIDED the employee's salary does not exceed 310 UVT (COP 16,235,940 per month in 2026). Where the monthly payments exceed 41 UVT (COP 2,147,334 in 2026), THE EXCESS is taxable income of the employee and is withheld as employment income. The instruction guide adds that the rule does not apply to company representation expenses, which remain deductible. Do NOT include amounts already in casilla 36. CLIENT EVIDENCE: meal payments to third parties are wage type 65818 Meal Allowance Inf.-2079, available per employee per month (non-zero in all 12 months of the Accumulated Report). Run the test MONTH BY MONTH per employee: the month's meal payment against 41 UVT and the employee's monthly salary against 310 UVT, using the UVT parameter of the tax year (52,374 for 2026); do NOT read the UVT from the accumulated client wage type 58001 UVT, which is not always the UVT (it is doubled or altered in months with two payroll runs or retro runs). The casilla is the sum of the monthly excesses over the tax year.
edits.reason: Verifier correction applied: the UVT must come from the tax-year parameter, not from wage type 58001, whose accumulated value is 2 x UVT or another value in 30 payee-months of 2026.
